newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: Czech PX50 closes down 1.8 points at 499.4.
newsitem.headline: Czech PX50 closes down 1.8 points at 499.4.

text.p: The Prague Stock Exchange's PX50 index of leading shares closed lower on Thursday, despite gains by IPB bank after the government said Nomura International could buy a 36 percent stake.
The PX50 closed 1.8 points, 0.36 percent, lower at 499.4.
IPB rose seven crowns to 243 but dealers said volume was low. They said the stock was likley to climb further over the next few days but that sellers might then emerge.
"It will go up for a couple of days but I don't think it will reach 300 as it was a few weeks ago," said trader Vasek Lausman of Zivnostenska Banka.
Czech Finance Minister Ivan Pilip said Nomura would pay six billion crowns for the Nomura stake and then raise its basic capital by a further six billion crowns.
"We do not yet know what might be the dilution effect of the six billion and we do not know about the real state of the financials of IPB," said Radim Bajgar of ING Barings.
SPT Telecom, the weightiest component in the index, fell 33 crowns to 3,635 and Komercni Banka, another heavyweight, closed 27 lower at 1,578.
"There was some demand for Komercni at the end of the day but people are overall a little pessimistic about Komercni's results," said Bajgar.
